policy_title: Reform the House of Lords and Civil Service leadership
stated: Reform UK will replace the House of Lords with a smaller, more democratic second chamber, with its structure to be debated and an immediate end to political appointees. They will replace Civil Service leaders with successful professionals from the private sector who are political appointees and come and go with the government.

source.quote: Commence Reform of the House of Lords & Civil Service Replace the crony-filled House of Lords with a much smaller, more democratic second chamber. Structure to be debated. Immediate end of political appointees. Replace Civil Service leaders with successful professionals from the private sector, who are political appointees, who come and go with the government.

bearing_set.reason: Both elements directly affect the democratic/constitutional structure: replacing the Lords with an elected chamber touches democratic and voting rights, while politicising civil service leadership (making permanent secretaries partisan appointees) touches rule-of-law and due-process safeguards that the independent civil service is designed to underpin.

membership_note: Both components are machinery-of-government changes but with real O9 stakes: one improves democratic accountability, the other risks degrading rule-of-law/due-process safeguards. Effects on other fundamentals (e.g. O13 via government effectiveness, O5 via security continuity) are too speculative to clear the non-negligible bar without a pinned mechanism and indicator.
